title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 54
paragraphs: After making these presents to the men of Delphi, Croesus consulted the Oracle a third time, for from the moment he had learned the truth of the Oracle he made abundant use of it. And consulting the Oracle, he inquired whether his monarchy would endure for a long time. The Pythian prophetess answered him thus:
“But when it comes to pass that a mule shall be king of the Medes, then, by the pebbly Hermus, O delicate-footed Lydian, flee and do not stay, and be not ashamed to be called a coward.”
